external_source: causaldata `snow` (Snow 1855), via NickCH-K/causaldata (MIT) — external anchor is the historical finding (direction only), not a scalar

local_attempt.note: Failed on complexity mismatch, not on the identification logic: the drafted plan reached for a full ML-style pipeline (categorical encoding of `supplier`/`treatment`, then the native gads_causal_estimate_ate DoWhy node) on a 4-row aggregated dataset, and the categorical-encoding transform failed on 'unknown categories in column 0' — a train/test-split-style failure mode that a 4-row table cannot support. Cloud, on this identical (and easiest-in-the-batch) spec, did a straightforward before/after DiD comparison and got the direction right. See notes.md.

estimate.note: GADS canonical from cloud reference run (drafted lane, DiD comparing 1849 vs 1854 across suppliers): clean water associated with a reduction of 56.9 deaths per 10,000 (40.13% relative to the counterfactual trend). This is a GADS-established reference value, not an external gold — causaldata carries no scalar answer for this case (see notes.md). Direction matches the historical finding (contaminated water increases mortality); magnitude has no external check.
